facts.text: The white-plumed honeyeater gets its name from the white neck-plumes that band its neck.
facts.quote: the distinguishing feature of the White-plumed honeyeater is the distil white bands at its neck called neck-plumes. This is where its name is derived from

facts.text: It is a medium-sized honeyeater with a yellowish head, pale grey-brown underparts and yellowish-olive feathers on its back.
facts.quote: It is a medium-sized honeyeater with a yellowish head, pale grey-brown plumage below and yellowish-olive feathers on its back.

facts.text: Its brush-tipped tongue has about 60 bristles that mop up nectar from flowers.
facts.quote: The tongue contains brush-like filaments, consisting of about 60 bristles, which are capable of mopping up nectar.

facts.text: Outside the breeding season it gathers in groups of 12 or more birds.
facts.quote: This is a gregarious species, often found in groups of 12 or more individuals during the nonbreeding season, which then dissipate during breeding.

facts.text: Breeding males perform a song flight, climbing and undulating above the treetops before diving into a tree.
facts.quote: Males undertake a song flight display, with a slight climbing and undulating flight above treetops while singing. At the song's completion, the male dives quickly into a nearby tree.

facts.text: The female weaves a cup nest from grasses and bark strips, bound with spider webs and lined with hair, wool and feathers.
facts.quote: These are skillfully woven from grasses and fine bark strips, bound with spider webs, and lined with animal hair, wool, and feathers.

facts.text: Eggs hatch after 13-15 days of incubation, and both parents feed the chicks for 11-15 days in the nest.
facts.quote: Incubation of eggs is most likely solely by the female for a period of 13–15 days. Both parents feed the offspring during the nestling period of 11–15 days

facts.text: Its nests are parasitised by pallid and fan-tailed cuckoos and by bronze-cuckoos.
facts.quote: The nests are parasitized by pallid (Cacomantis pallidus) and fan-tailed cuckoos (Cacomantis flabelliformis) and Horsfield's (Chrysococcyx basalis) and shining bronze-cuckoos (Chrysococcyx lucidus).

facts.text: It has a strong association with River Red Gums and favours woodlands and riverside areas.
facts.quote: White-Plumed Honeyeaters exhibit a preference for woodlands and riparian areas and have a very strong association with River Red Gums.
